paper_metadata.title: A Novel Decomposition-Ensemble Approach for Forecasting Stock Price With Quantum Neural Network and Big Data

summary: The paper proposes a MEMD-QNN framework for forecasting the Shenzhen Stock Exchange average price using 2267 trading-day samples and three feature groups: technical indicators, Baidu search query data, and Weibo sentiment. The best reported test performance is for MEMD-QNN with all features: MAE 0.2410, RMSE 0.2996, and MAPE 0.0185, compared with QNN at 0.6099/0.7385/0.0457 and classical baselines such as BPNN at 1.7255/1.7852/0.1295 and SVR at 1.7030/1.7259/0.1290 in the three-feature setting.

experiments.description: MEMD-QNN stock price forecasting on Shenzhen Stock Exchange average price using technical indicators, Baidu search query data, and Weibo sentiment; compared against QNN, MEMD-BPNN, MEMD-SVR, MEMD-ELM, BPNN, SVR, and ELM.

algorithm.variant: QNN / quantum circuit learning with A2-CNOT encoding and z-axis measurement
algorithm.ansatz: A2-CNOT encoding with repeated quantum layers (CNOT-XZX shape)

hyperparameters.optimizer_updates: 10 times the training parameters in quantum layers are updated

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input features are encoded as rotation angles in RY and RZ gates; number of qubits set to twice the number of features
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize fidelity-based loss between measured output state and all-zero state; forecast next-day average stock price

problem_instance.description: Forecast daily average stock price of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange using market indicators, search query data, and social media sentiment
problem_instance.dataset_name: Shenzhen Stock Exchange average price dataset with Wind, Baidu Index, and Weibo features

dataset_specification.description: Trading days from 2013-12-02 to 2023-03-23; average price computed as daily total trading value divided by trading volume; features include technical indicators, aggregated search query data (SQD), and sentiment scores from Weibo posts; 9:1 train-test split

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Remove suspended days; align features with stock price; normalize all series to [0,1]; de-duplicate Weibo posts; remove URLs/non-Chinese characters; convert emojis to text; remove stop words; segment Chinese text with jieba; fine-tune BERT for sentiment scoring; average Weibo sentiment scores between 3 p.m. across two trading days; MEMD decomposition of stock price and features
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 independent training/forecasting runs; out-of-sample testing; metrics MAE, RMSE, MAPE; Diebold-Mariano test

implementation_details.classical_solver: Adam optimizer; classical baselines include SVR, BPNN, ELM
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: MEMD decomposition, normalization, feature selection, BERT-based sentiment extraction, correlation analysis
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Ensemble by summing predictions from separate QNN models; inverse normalization; compute MAE/RMSE/MAPE and DM test

speedup_claims.factor: best MAPE 0.0185 vs 0.0293-0.1728 across classical baselines
speedup_claims.baseline_method: BPNN, SVR, ELM, MEMD-BPNN, MEMD-SVR, MEMD-ELM
speedup_claims.conditions: testing set; technical index + SQD + sentiment score; averaged over 20 runs
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an empirical accuracy improvement, not an asymptotic computational speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: 33.70% improvement after adding SQD; 42.60% improvement after adding sentiment score
speedup_claims.caveats: Improvement rates are reported in the paper; exact denominator is the prior feature set performance.

speedup_claims.factor: 34.46% improvement after adding SQD; 26.36% improvement after adding sentiment score
speedup_claims.caveats: Empirical feature contribution, not a computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware resource estimate is reported; the paper is algorithmic and compares only forecast errors on a 2267-sample financial time series.
limiting_factors: No quantum hardware or device execution is reported
No asymptotic complexity or crossover analysis is provided
The paper reports empirical forecast improvements, not a computational advantage over classical methods
Classical baselines are strong and in some settings close to QNN/MEMD-QNN

notes: Paper reports the QNN uses A2-CNOT encoding, with the number of qubits set to twice the number of features, and uses 5 layers for three features, 3 layers for two features, and 1 layer for one feature. Exact total qubit count is not explicitly given because the paper describes it parametrically by feature count rather than a single fixed number.
No specific hardware, simulator, framework, or transpilation details are reported; the experiment is described algorithmically only.
The paper claims superior empirical performance of QNN/MEMD-QNN over classical baselines, but does not establish an asymptotic quantum speedup order.
The authors claim superior forecasting accuracy for MEMD-QNN, with best reported MAPE 0.0185, RMSE 0.2996, and MAE 0.2410 on the three-feature setting.
However, the paper does not establish a Hoefler-style practical quantum advantage, does not report hardware execution, and provides no complexity crossover analysis.

experiments.description: Classical benchmark models are reported as part of the same forecasting experiment and should be captured as classical_baselines rather than separate quantum experiments: BPNN, SVR, and ELM, plus their MEMD variants MEMD-BPNN, MEMD-SVR, and MEMD-ELM.
